openings.claim: The tighter fit may restrain motion while making exchange seating depend on friction or clamp-induced rocking. Replace that dependency with deliberate seating against fixed corner contacts and an end stop before hand-tightening each rod's captive closing bar.
openings.delta: Propose two independently releasable plywood seats joined inside the envelope. Use supplied bolts and nuts for closing bars and end stops; cord and elastic loops retain every released component. Nearest rival: clearance dominates both load displacement and exchange error, so a tighter surrounding fit should improve both.
openings.prediction: If seating history dominates, the corner-seated configuration should reduce unloaded return error despite allowing insertion clearance. If clearance dominates, the tight-fit configuration should have smaller loaded displacement without worse return error. These are competing predictions, not measured effects; the two supplied trials establish neither explanation.
openings.probe: Reuse the supplied materials for at most two configurations: corner seating followed by closure, and tighter surrounding contact. For each, log twelve exchanges: first five of each original rod, then the specified 18 mm substitution for the last two. Record target return and exchange time each time; conduct four ten-second 10 N trials after exchanges 5, 10, 11 and 12. Keep base and pointer attachment unchanged. Reject the candidate if return or loaded position leaves the 2 mm circle, any exchange reaches forty seconds, or retention fails. Fabrication exceeding 100 minutes or testing exceeding twenty defeats this probe's capacity; a time cap alone establishes no feasibility.
assumptions: Six plywood pieces and eight bolts can realize both seats, retention and stops within 90 mm; hardware lengths and frame geometry are unspecified.
Hand tightening supplies sufficient restraint without damaging rods; clamp force and friction are unknown.
Corner referencing can preserve the pointer datum after changing rod width; the 18 mm substitution can defeat this premise.

assessment: One discriminating opening. It preserves all requirements as acceptance conditions; fabrication, stiffness and substitution compatibility remain unproven. Probe only, with no deployment claim.
